extracted.intended_audience: administrators, Title IX coordinators, and compliance officers at recipients of Federal education funds (schools, colleges, universities)
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX notice and training requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for a recipient's notice of nondiscrimination, publication of that notice, and mandatory training for employees and Title IX personnel under the Department's final Title IX regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures applicability in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's notice of nondiscrimination must state that its grievance procedures apply to resolution of complaints made by students, employees, or other individuals who are participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that grievance procedures are not limited to employee complaints; whether a postdoctoral trainee is an employee is fact-specific, but trainees participating/attempting to participate would likely be entitled to make a complaint. The Department also clarifies that complainants are not required to exhaust administrative remedies with the recipient before filing with OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents: where to locate policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include information on how to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy and its grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules consolidate the requirement to state where to find both the nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures into the same paragraph (final §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D)). The Department deleted redundant cross-references (e.g., to §§106.45 and 106.46) where coverage is implied by reference to grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to include proof of training in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of nondiscrimination is not required to include proof that the recipient has completed Title IX training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are subject to training requirements under §106.8(d), but requiring proof in the notice would force frequent updates and impose unnecessary burdens; the Department declines to add such a requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'attempting to participate' wording (scope of coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory language uses 'attempting to participate' rather than 'applying' to define third parties who may be covered by grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'attempting to participate' is broader and includes people who applied, withdrew but desire to re-enroll, or otherwise try to access a program; replacing it with 'applying' would narrow coverage inappropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional inclusion of exemptions (e.g., religious) in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may include information in its notice about exceptions or exemptions applicable under Title IX (such as the statutory religious exemption), but is not required to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice language appropriately limits coverage to obligations the recipient is 'required by Title IX and this part' to comply with. Requiring recipients to assert or explain religious exemptions would be impractical and fact-specific; recipients may, but need not, include qualifying language about exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication locations for notice of nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must publish its notice of nondiscrimination in handbooks, catalogs, announcements, bulletins, application forms, and on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.8(c)(2) restores the longstanding requirement (from 1975 until 2020) to publish the notice in these materials to increase awareness but accounts for space/format limits by allowing a short-form notice when necessary. Publication may be in the same medium the materials are distributed (print vs. electronic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form notice allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: When space or format limits require it, a recipient may provide a shorter version of the notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The short-form may be a one-sentence statement that the recipient prohibits sex discrimination and that individuals may report concerns to the Title IX Coordinator, plus a link to the full notice on the website. This provides minimum necessary information without undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and meaningful access considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure the notice of nondiscrimination is widely accessible to the school community, including individuals with limited English proficiency and individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes additional barriers for low-income, transient, LEP, and disabled populations and requires publication in both print materials and online; however, Title IX does not restate obligations under other laws (e.g., Title VI, Section 504), and recipients remain responsible for complying with those separate accessibility obligations. Recipients have discretion in drafting accessible wording and formats and may post notices in public locations or at events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training required for all employees
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be trained on the recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination, the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination (including 'sex-based harassment'), and all applicable notification and information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(d)(1) requires training of all employees (not merely making training available). The Department expects training to be incorporated into existing annual trainings where feasible and rejects exceptions for classes of employees (e.g., short-term substitutes) as a general rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted training for investigators, decisionmakers, and implementers
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and other personnel responsible for implementing grievance procedures or modifying/terminating supportive measures must receive role-specific training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(d)(2) requires training on the recipient's obligations under §106.44; the recipient's grievance procedures under §106.45 (and §106.46, if applicable); how to serve impartially (avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, bias); the meaning and application of 'relevant' re: questions/evidence; and types of evidence that are impermissible regardless of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for informal resolution facilitators
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators of informal resolution processes must be trained on rules and practices associated with informal resolution and on how to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(d)(3) requires training that addresses process rules and impartiality, including avoiding conflicts of interest and bias when facilitating informal resolution under §106.44(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Title IX Coordinators and designees
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators and their designees must be trained on their specific responsibilities under the regulations, the recipient's recordkeeping system, and other training necessary to coordinate compliance with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training topics include responsibilities under §§106.8(a), 106.40(b)(3), 106.44(f), 106.44(g), and §106.8(f) recordkeeping requirements, as well as any additional training necessary to coordinate Title IX compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training frequency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons required to receive training must be trained promptly upon hiring or upon a change of position that alters their Title IX duties, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.8(d) to specify prompt training upon hiring or duty changes and annual retraining, preserving recipient flexibility in how training is structured while ensuring personnel remain informed of obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality, bias prohibitions in training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training must instruct personnel to serve impartially and must not rely on sex stereotypes; it must address avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations (e.g., §106.8(d)(2)(iii)) mandate training on impartiality and prohibit training materials or practices that rely on sex stereotypes. The final rule also includes procedural safeguards (conflict-of-interest requirements, equitable treatment mandates, and appeal rights when bias is alleged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make training materials available for public inspection upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(f) requires that a recipient's training materials be available for public inspection, providing accountability and enabling OCR or others to review compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of who must be trained (employees vs. non-employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training is required for all employees; advisors, graduate students, contractors, volunteers, and third-party agents must be trained only if they are employees or directly involved in carrying out the recipient's Title IX duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate training for non-employees who are not directly involved in carrying out Title IX duties, though recipients may choose to train volunteers/contractors/third parties where appropriate. Whether an individual is an 'employee' can vary by circumstance and state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in training content and methods (but no substitutions for mandated topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion in selecting training materials, trainers, and specific practices beyond the topics mandated by §106.8(d), but must meet the regulatory training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not require recipients to hire outside trainers or adopt particular training techniques. It leaves optional topics (e.g., trauma-informed practices) to recipients' discretion, while noting some commenters' concerns that certain optional topics could introduce bias. The Department declines to require additional mandated topics beyond those in §106.8(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: No general exceptions to training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to adopt exceptions to training requirements (e.g., for small entities or temporary employees); training all employees is required as a condition of receiving Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While acknowledging resource/time burdens, the Department determined benefits outweigh costs and notes flexibility in how training is delivered. The final rules take effect August 1, 2024, giving recipients time to plan and implement required training and policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for training and regulatory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations, including training requirements, are effective August 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered implementation burdens and provided this effective date to allow recipients sufficient time to plan, amend policies, procedures, and trainings as necessary.
